duplicate_conflict_rule.applies_to: two or more rows of the authoritative source sharing one identity_fields triple but carrying different impact labels
duplicate_conflict_rule.rule: the highest impact_rank wins; the losing labels are recorded on the collapsed row and counted in the run self-report
duplicate_conflict_rule.rationale: A news filter is a safety device. On an identity conflict the fail-safe direction is the more restrictive classification, never the milder one: blocking a window that did not need blocking costs one skipped trade, trading through a window that should have been blocked costs an unbounded tail. Contract section 8 explicitly permits visible deduplication under a recorded rule, so the escalation is logged rather than silent.
duplicate_conflict_rule.unresolvable: two different labels of equal rank remain a hard DuplicateEventConflict - there is no fail-safe direction to pick

known_conflicts_at_decision_time.note: the only conflicting identity in the 48727-row canonical file as of 2026-09-13; it previously made run_self_report refuse the canonical source outright

known_at_utc_policy.provenance: Neither calendar seed (news_calendar_2015_2025.csv, forex_factory_calendar_clean.csv) carries a 'when this row was first published' column, so known_at_utc cannot be measured for the historical backfill. This is therefore a documented estimate, never a measurement, and never silently equal to timestamp_utc (which would misrepresent every historical event as an unscheduled same-instant surprise). lead_hours is deliberately the same small, conservative 24h across all labels: no differentiated upstream evidence exists to justify a longer or per-label-distinct lead time, and inventing one would violate the no-invented-values rule this contract itself sets (section 6). A future ingestion pass with real publication timestamps supersedes this policy_id, not this file in place.
